audit.reasoning: Coding 'fixed-dominant', final stress (final stress, not in the strict set) matches Lobel 2016 exactly: stress non-contrastive, regularly word-final, a few unpredictable penultimate exceptions. The quotation is verified verbatim at p. 399 of the open LD&C PDF (now, identical to the Aug-31 scan copy). The source is first-hand and modern (the documenter of the last speakers), so nothing suggests the classification is wrong; but the record's cite/loc/grade fields are blank and the catalog 'held' list is empty, so the action is to register the copy we hold, add locator 'p. 399', and set an strength of the evidence. sources.citation: Lobel 2016, Ponosakan: The Sounds of a Silently Dying Language of Indonesia, LD&C 10 (full downloaded from ScholarSpace API, sole stress passage read)
sources.quote: As in other Mongondow-Gorontalo languages, stress is not contrastive in Ponosakan, and regularly falls on word-final syllables, with a few unpredictable exceptions where it falls on the penultimate syllable, e.g., si'ene [si'?ene] 'who'.
